issues.failure_explanation: In the proof, the term \tilde I_i originates from the l-th power of a sum, expanded over ORDERED tuples (Upsilon_1,...,Upsilon_l) of LN-trees (eq. (4.13)); LN-trees have ordered branches (fig_equal_tree: permuting branches gives a different LN-tree, eq. fig_equal_tree), so the map 'ordered tuple of branches -> composed LN-tree' is bijective: each LN-tree (Upsilon_1...Upsilon_l)_k arises from exactly one tuple. Nevertheless, part (iv) re-indexes the tuple sum as sum over LN-trees weighted by N_P(Upsilon) (the number of permutations FIXING the ordered tuple, Definition def_order), i.e., it counts each tree N_P times instead of once; grouping by classes then gives class multiplicity alpha instead of alpha/N_P. Hence the coefficient claimed in (eq2_Rnj_indc) equals alpha*S/gamma, while the true Taylor coefficient is alpha*S/(gamma*N_P). Example: for the cherry ([;]_1[;]_1)_0 the class is a singleton (alpha=1, N_P=2, S=2, gamma=2); the second-order Taylor term (1/2!)(Delta t)^4 (F^{[;]_1}.d_theta)^2 F contributes exactly (1/2)(S/gamma)([;]_1)^2 per tuple and only one tuple exists, so the true coefficient of the class is (1/2)*A_0^m(Upsilon) (times the k-Taylor factor), not the stated alpha*S/gamma = 1 times A_0^m(Upsilon). The same factor error affects every tree having two or more equivalent branches at a common parent; the smallest one, [[;]_0[;]_0]_0, has order 3, so the stated expansion is false for every r >= 3 (for arbitrary coefficients, as the theorem assumes). The single-node base case (N_P=1) and all asymmetric trees are stated correctly.

issues.overall_effect: The exact coefficients alpha(Υ)S/gamma in the paper's central error expansion (Theorem thm_taylor) are wrong by the factor N_P(Upsilon) for all ULN-trees possessing a nontrivial branch symmetry, first occurring at order 3 ([[;]_0[;]_0]_0). Only the values of the coefficients are affected: the set of trees and the fact that R^{n}=O((Delta t)^{r+1}) whenever A_0^m(Upsilon)=0 are untouched, so the order conditions C(r) (eq_defCr, thm_consistent), Proposition prop_Cr_table, and the convergence results remain valid.
issues.title: Error expansion of Theorem thm_taylor overcounts trees with symmetric branches by the factor N_P
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of one combinatorial factor in one displayed formula plus the adjacent regrouping sentence; the corrected expansion is equally strong, and every order condition, consistency, and convergence guarantee of the paper survives unchanged because they depend only on which coefficients A_0^m(Upsilon) vanish, not on their values.
